dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: I'm gonna have to get my hands on "that thing" if I want to make a killing... Like they say, the bigger the risk, the greater the reward!

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but we ain't open for business right now.

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: I was doing business on the train earlier when the attendant came along and told me I was in violation of some regulation or another... It's a darn good thing I'd just sold the last of my wares, ha ha!

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: So now, I don't have any good stuff on hand, unfortunately. Please come back again another time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mentioned "that thing" just now. So what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: Mind you, the attendant's still watching. Better not mention anything those Transport Bureau pen-pushers will squint at.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: Oh! I'm sorry, but we ain't open for business right now. Please come back again next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you mean it's something illegal...

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: Tsaritsa have pity on me! I never said that, you did.

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: From what I know, some of those gangs do deal in... what would you call... the more, um, irregular stuff. And they go to great lengths just to move that thing.

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: They're even willing to pay—— Ahem. I mean, that's what they say. As you can imagine, word gets around fast among folks like me.

dialogues.speaker: Aivazovsky
dialogues.text: But why are you asking about this? I'm telling you, getting past the Transport Bureau's checks isn't exactly child's play. So whatever it is you've got in mind, you'd better drop it now.
